falsifiers: fewer than 4 clear -> a subject was not actually the whole blocker set for that row
more than 4 clear -> the change reached beyond moe_routing, or a cluster boundary is wrong
any GREEN row regresses -> not a remediation
BUG > 0 or a silent drop appears -> do not merge
K3 cluster count moves off 7 -> unrelated work is being credited to K3

result.diagnosis: The wave shipped TWO changes, and only one was moe_routing. (a) The expert schedule (decoder_sparse_step / mlp_only_layers judged by value) is moe_routing proper, and cleared exactly the two Qwen3-MoE rows. (b) The null-declaration rule — a key declared with no value has nothing to carry — is a CROSS-CUTTING census rule. It cleared the two Gemma 4 dense rows, whose blocking subjects happened to be moe-clustered, AND OLMoE-1B-7B, whose blocker clip_qkv: null sits in attention_bias. So moe_routing proper cleared 2, not 4.
result.lesson: A cluster names what a blocker is ABOUT, not which fix will clear it. clears_alone is exact only when the remediation is confined to one cluster. A cross-cutting rule breaks the cluster->fix mapping in both directions: it over-credits the cluster it was filed under and under-predicts rows elsewhere. Future forecasts must state the FIX being made, not only the cluster.
